database.title: Where should this platform keep its data?
database.help: Asked first because nothing else can be stored until it is answered. This is the one choice here that cannot be changed later in Settings.
database.restartWarning: Choosing this restarts the platform so it can connect. It takes about twenty seconds, and this page waits for it. The passwords are generated for you and stored on the server — you never have to type them.
database.claimedByOther: Someone else reached this installation first and is setting it up. If that was not you, restart the platform to start again.
database.failed: The database could not be configured. Please try again.
database.restartTimeout: The platform is taking longer than expected to restart. Your database settings were saved — reload this page to continue.

postgres.name: PostgreSQL
postgres.note: Recommended. Runs one site or many, keeping each site's data separate at the database level.

sqlite.name: SQLite
sqlite.note: One file, no database server to run. This installation will only ever serve a single site — it has no way to keep two sites' data apart.

mysql.name: MySQL
mysql.note: A database server you already run. Keeps roles and backups like PostgreSQL, but has no way to keep two sites' data apart — so this installation will only ever serve a single site. Not included in this stack: point it at your own server.

database.ownerRoleHelp: This driver keeps each site's data separate, which needs two roles: one that owns the tables and runs migrations, and one that serves requests and owns nothing. Serving requests as the owner turns that separation off without any error. Both must already exist on your server.

domain.title: The admin's domain
domain.adminUrlHelp: Prefilled with whatever you are using right now — a bare IP is fine until DNS is ready. This is what the platform routes the admin by, so change it only if you will reach it somewhere else, and point that domain here first.
domain.unclaimedWarning: This installation has not been claimed yet. Until you finish, anyone who can reach it can set it up instead of you. It stops accepting setup 15 minutes after starting.

general.frontendUrlMultiSite: On a multi-site platform, leave it blank. A value here is read before the request is, so it replaces every site’s own domain everywhere in that list. Blank falls back to FRONTEND_URL in the environment, then to the host that made the request — which is how each site gets its own address.
general.adminUrlFallback: Blank falls back to ADMIN_URL in the environment, then to the host that made the request. Unlike the two above, this one belongs to the platform, however many sites it serves.
general.siteUrlMultiSite: On a multi-site platform, leave it blank, for the same reason as Frontend URL.
general.marketplaceUrlSite: Where THIS site browses for plugins and themes. Blank uses the platform’s marketplace; off turns this site’s marketplace off. A catalogue that cannot be reached shows an empty marketplace rather than an error.
general.marketplaceUrlPlatform: Where the platform browses for plugins, themes and appearances, and checks for updates, and what every site that has not set its own uses. Blank uses the default marketplace; off turns the marketplace off.
general.frameworkRepositoryDescription: Checked for new framework releases when no marketplace answers. owner/repo on GitHub — point it at your own fork if you run one. Blank uses {{repository}}.
general.sourcesWorkspaceDescription: Where Sources clones repositories and writes the packages it builds. Blank uses data/sources beside the platform. Never point it at the plugins or themes directories — that is where the sources being built are mounted from.
general.indexPlatformHostsDescription: Let search engines index this admin console, every workspace console, and every api. host.
general.indexNotStorefronts: Does not apply to the storefront sites you host — each follows its own “Visible to” setting under Sites, and nothing here changes it.
general.indexOff: Off — those hosts answer robots.txt with Disallow: /, and every response carries X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow, noarchive.
general.indexOn: On — they answer Allow: / and send no such header.
general.brandedSignUpEmailDescription: The email a visitor gets to verify their address after signing up. Off: the plain framework email. On: this site’s own copy below, signed with the Platform Name. {{brandName}} in any line is replaced with it.
